annotations.text:
WHAT THIS BOARD IS
One screen: the chat, where someone asks a question about the agreement in plain English. This is a single design, already agreed — nothing here is asking you to choose between options.

The two boards below the main screen are ZOOMED DETAILS of parts that are CLOSED by default. They are not separate screens. You only see them if you click.

WHO IT IS FOR
Someone who needs an answer out of a 475-page agreement and has no interest in how the system works.

WHAT CHANGED THIS ROUND
· Far less on screen. The answer is a plain column of text with nothing competing with it. No rail of statistics, no visible trace.
· Citations are now numbered footnotes, one per claim, instead of paths crowded into the sentence.
· Clicking a footnote opens ONE panel on the right — the page image and the exact words. That panel is the only place evidence appears.
· Highlighted terms stay, and are deliberately a different shape from footnotes: a filled pill opens a definition, a small raised number opens evidence.
· The trace is closed, and opens as a flow you can read rather than a log.
· New: “See the connections” opens a map of the provisions behind the answer, numbered to match the footnotes.

WHAT I WOULD VALUE YOUR EYES ON
1. Is the answer text itself pitched right — plain enough, short enough?
2. Footnote number vs filled pill: is the difference obvious without being told?
3. Is the connections map worth the space it takes?

ON THE TWO DETAIL BOARDS BELOW
Left: what opens when you click “How I found this”. Written as steps in ordinary words — what was looked for and what came back — rather than tool names and timings.

Right: what opens when you click “See the connections”. Dark ground, one glowing provision where the answer starts, dashed lines out to what it depends on. The numbers on the nodes are the same numbers as the footnotes in the answer. A dashed, dimmed node is something the system could not settle — shown rather than hidden.

ON THE VISUAL STYLING
Now built in the Whitespace product register from the brand memo: a neutral near-black ground, cards a step up from it, one flat action blue for anything you can act on, Inter for text and JetBrains Mono for references and page numbers. Status is a small pill, never a wash across a row.

The marketing lavender and the gradient appear only where the memo allows them: the soft glow in the corner behind the composer, and the connectors on the connections view. Nothing else borrows from the marketing look.

British English throughout, sentence case on product labels.

HOW WE GOT HERE — reference only, no decision needed.

Three ways of attaching evidence to a claim were sketched before the first build. A (inline chips) was chosen then, and built.

On seeing it working, the chips proved too dense: a path and a page number inside every sentence competes with the sentence. So this round moved to C, numbered footnotes, with the evidence in a single panel — which is also the pattern the reference chat UI settled on.

A is kept here because it was the earlier decision and the reasoning for changing it only makes sense beside it. Nothing on this page needs your approval.
